critical_operation.code:
FROM node:22-bookworm

RUN corepack enable

WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_OPTIONS="--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning"

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.json tsdown.config.ts vitest.config.ts vitest.e2e.config.ts openclaw.mjs ./
COPY src ./src
COPY test ./test
COPY scripts ./scripts
COPY docs ./docs
COPY skills ./skills
COPY patches ./patches
COPY ui ./ui
COPY extensions/memory-core ./extensions/memory-core

RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
RUN pnpm build
RUN pnpm ui:build

CMD ["bash"]
critical_operation.desc: Lines 1-23 are the vulnerable configuration interval. The Dockerfile starts from a root-default Node image, copies and builds the app, and registers CMD ["bash"] without ever declaring USER. The bug is the structural absence of a non-root boundary, so marking only CMD would hide the root cause.

entry_point.desc: The FROM instruction introduces the base image default root user into the Dockerfile state. Because no later USER instruction narrows that identity, root remains active through the build steps and the final CMD; for this missing-USER configuration bug, the first FROM line is the entry point.

critical_operation.code:
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim

RUN apt-get update \
  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    bash \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    git \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY run.sh /usr/local/bin/openclaw-install-e2e
RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/openclaw-install-e2e

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/openclaw-install-e2e"]
critical_operation.desc: Lines 1-14 are the vulnerable configuration interval. The Dockerfile installs system packages, copies an installer into /usr/local/bin, marks it executable, and registers it as ENTRYPOINT while never switching away from root. The root cause is the missing USER boundary across the complete file.

entry_point.desc: The FROM instruction selects a root-default Node slim image. With no later USER instruction, that default identity becomes the active identity for package installation, script placement, chmod, and the container entrypoint.

critical_operation.code:
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash app \
  && echo "app ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" > /etc/sudoers.d/app

USER app
critical_operation.desc: Lines 17-20 are the vulnerable configuration interval. The Dockerfile creates app, grants it NOPASSWD:ALL through sudoers, and then switches to USER app. That switch only looks like a downgrade: app can regain root without a password, so the non-root boundary is ineffective.

entry_point.desc: This RUN starts the non-root boundary by creating app. In this variant the defect is not simply missing USER; the app boundary is immediately invalidated by the adjacent sudoers grant, so the user-creation block is the configuration entry point.

trace.code:
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash app \
  && echo "app ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" > /etc/sudoers.d/app

USER app
trace.desc: Configuration state: app is created, given passwordless full sudo, and then selected as USER. These adjacent instructions together erase the intended privilege boundary.
Privilege proof: after USER app, the build still uses sudo to chmod a system path, demonstrating that the app user can exercise root.
Runtime materialization: the nonroot-named entrypoint runs as app, but that app identity carries passwordless full-root escalation.
